findings.title: Reject unresolved numeric references and invalid decoded characters before issuing canonical names
findings.trigger: A well-formed Protein XML common-name contains escaped malformed numeric markup such as protein &#-1;, extra-escaped numeric markup such as protein &amp;#946;, or an escaped numeric reference to U+FFFF (protein &#xFFFF;).
findings.observed: HTMLParser treats the malformed numeric form as ordinary data and the final label guard only checks named entities. A valid numeric reference to U+FFFF passes the 32..10FFFF/non-surrogate range check. The parser emits protein &#-1;, protein β or a literal U+FFFF as a canonical name. Two independent actual CLI builds (malformed numeric and U+FFFF) exit 0 and replace a prior output sentinel.
findings.expected: Malformed/unresolved numeric markup and disallowed decoded character values fail before term emission; CLI retains existing output, or creates no output. Ordinary escaped beta/numeric beta and the four native source labels still succeed.
findings.impact: The newly advertised resolved-name guard can publish malformed native authority labels. This is a parser-contract defect demonstrated with synthetic mutations; the four intended original bodies are unaffected.
findings.cause: handle_data retains unrecognized numeric-reference syntax; the final residual-entity check omits numeric references, and handle_charref permits U+FFFF.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the final decoded label for residual numeric-reference syntax and invalid characters, without recursive unescaping or chemical-name rewriting; add direct and CLI failure-before-write regression cases.

passed_checks: Four independently rehashed untouched original XML bodies emit exactly the expected four native canonical labels and no aliases.
Duplicate query/species fields, wrong ID/database version, missing direct name, wrong datatype, nested-name fallback, wrong service host and malformed tags reject.

DTD declarations reject in UTF-8 and UTF-16 via the explicit callback. Explicit UTF-16-LE/BE encoding-name fixtures fail at decoder support before content use; no claim that these exercised the callback.
Actual XML/HTML canonical-name conflicts fail in both manifest orders and preserve prior authority-output bytes.
AST comparison confirms all prior parser functions and main unchanged; only source_terms and build_snapshot existing definitions changed, plus four new definitions.
Reviewed complete three-file implementation and original-source support assessment.
Final reviewed owned-file and archived-file digests match author sealed handoff.

execution.meaning: Probe script completed and recorded outcomes; this is not a claim that every negative case was rejected.
